title: Restore Etcd Snapshot & Reconfigure Manifest
prompt:
A pre-captured etcd snapshot exists on `controlplane` at `/opt/cka-restore/snap.db`. You must verify disaster-recovery procedures by restoring this snapshot into a clean data directory.

Perform the following tasks:
1. Restore the etcd snapshot `/opt/cka-restore/snap.db` on `controlplane` to data directory `/var/lib/etcd-restore`.
2. Update `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml` so etcd mounts and uses `/var/lib/etcd-restore` as its `etcd-data` hostPath.
3. Wait for `etcd` and the Kubernetes API server to recover cleanly and confirm ConfigMap `restore-anchor` and Secret `restore-secret` exist in namespace `cka-etcd-restore`.
hints: Extract `--name`, `--initial-cluster`, and `--initial-advertise-peer-urls` from `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`, then run `sudo etcdutl snapshot restore /opt/cka-restore/snap.db --name=<name> --initial-cluster=<cluster> --initial-advertise-peer-urls=<peer> --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restore`.

manifests:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: restore-anchor
  namespace: cka-etcd-restore
data:
  status: snapshotted
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: restore-secret
  namespace: cka-etcd-restore
stringData:
  token: snapshotted

node_commands.command: rm -r -f /opt/cka-restore /var/lib/etcd-restore && mkdir -p /opt/cka-restore && ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save /opt/cka-restore/snap.db

checks.description: Restored etcd member directory exists at `/var/lib/etcd-restore/member`

node_commands.command: rm -r -f /var/lib/etcd-restore && NAME=$(grep -oE -- '--name=[^" ]+' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml | head -n1 | cut -d= -f2-) && INIT_CLUSTER=$(grep -oE -- '--initial-cluster=[^" ]+' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml | head -n1 | cut -d= -f2-) && PEER_URLS=$(grep -oE -- '--initial-advertise-peer-urls=[^" ]+' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml | head -n1 | cut -d= -f2-) && (command -v etcdutl >/dev/null 2>&1 && etcdutl snapshot restore /opt/cka-restore/snap.db --name="$NAME" --initial-cluster="$INIT_CLUSTER" --initial-advertise-peer-urls="$PEER_URLS" --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restore || ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /opt/cka-restore/snap.db --name="$NAME" --initial-cluster="$INIT_CLUSTER" --initial-advertise-peer-urls="$PEER_URLS" --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restore) && sed -i 's|path: /var/lib/etcd$|path: /var/lib/etcd-restore|' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml && sleep 6 && for i in $(seq 1 35); do kubectl --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf get --raw=/readyz >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done

sed -i 's|path: /var/lib/etcd-restore|path: /var/lib/etcd|g' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml && rm -r -f /opt/cka-restore /var/lib/etcd-restore && sleep 6 && for i in $(seq 1 35); do kubectl --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf get --raw=/readyz >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done

reference_solution: Restore `/opt/cka-restore/snap.db` into `/var/lib/etcd-restore` with `--name`, `--initial-cluster`, and `--initial-advertise-peer-urls` matching `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml` using `etcdutl` (or `etcdctl`), then update `etcd-data` hostPath in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`.
